The approach to determining progression was not standardised across centres
Findings should ideally be confirmed in a prospective trial using NETPET as an exploratory endpoint, although accrual in an uncommon disease would be difficult
Larger numbers and longer follow-up are needed before concluding that NETPET further stratifies within histological grade, and to test it within well- and poorly differentiated grade 3
critique: Two of the three centres had already published their own NETPET series and the original 2017 derivation cohort came from one of them, so this is partly a re-analysis of the data that generated the hypothesis rather than external validation; a 239-patient interim version of this same cohort had already been presented in 2021
Only 36% of patients had pancreatic primaries and no pancreas-specific subgroup analysis is presented, so the score cannot be cited as evidence for managing pancreatic NET

Histological grade - the comparator the score is said to complement - was taken from whatever biopsy was available with no central pathology review across three countries, which biases the comparison in the index test's favour

The authors concede that treatment, including PRRT, was not modelled; since SSTR-positive/FDG-negative disease is the eligibility criterion for PRRT, the P1 advantage is confounded with access to an effective therapy

Time zero is the date of the second scan, which sits at an arbitrary and differing point in each patient's disease course and selects for patients who survived to be scanned, inviting left-truncation and immortal-time bias
The analysis again uses the pre-specified three-category collapse, so the 5-point scale the papers propose remains unvalidated at the level at which it is reported clinically

The finding that 59% of grade 1 patients were FDG-avid, well above published rates, is presented as a strength of dual imaging but is equally consistent with reader threshold drift or with grade misassignment, and is not resolved
36434154.n: 319 patients with metastatic or unresectable GEPNEN (114 pancreatic primaries, 36%)
36434154.bottom_line: In 319 patients with metastatic GEP-NEN the NETPET score independently predicted overall survival and time to progression alongside histological grade, but two of the three contributing centres supplied the original derivation data, treatment was not adjusted for, and only a third of the cohort had pancreatic primaries.
36434154.funding: No specific funding for the research project; D.L. Chan funded by NHMRC Australia grant GNT1175788. Several authors report honoraria or research support from Ipsen, Novartis, AAA, Pfizer, Lexicon, EMD Serono and others outside the submitted work.

limitations: Only resected PNET were included, so the study is subject to the selection bias that led patients to undergo resection, and the authors could not retrospectively ascertain which PNET were managed non-operatively

Some cystic PNET under 3 cm with non-mucinous cyst fluid may have been misdiagnosed as serous cystic lesions, so the true proportion of cystic PNET is probably misrepresented - though the authors argue that including them would strengthen the findings since the most favourable lesions are the ones least likely to be operated

Given the multicentre design, variation in radiographic imaging and interpretation, data collection, pathology assessment and treatment across institutions may exist, offset in the authors' view by greater generalisability and adequate sample size
critique: The multivariable hazard ratio for calcification is 11.5 with a confidence interval from 1.1 to 125.0 at p = 0.043 - a point estimate with essentially no precision - sitting in a model that also returns 25.2 and 33.0 for nodal and distant metastasis, the signature of an overfitted Cox model with far too few recurrence events for the covariates entered; no event count for the model is reported anywhere

Between 28% and 29% of the cohort has no data on the two exposures of interest and the analysis is complete-case with no imputation and no sensitivity analysis, so the effective sample is not 981 and may be differentially missing by centre and era

Table 1 is internally inconsistent, giving n = 167 cystic and 814 solid and 177 calcified and 804 non-calcified in one row against 120, 582, 122 and 575 in the column headers, with a garbled '305 (3)' cell - so the denominators underlying the percentages cannot be reconstructed from the paper

Imaging was classified from radiology report wording rather than by central re-read, across eight institutions and seventeen years of changing CT and MRI technique, which makes the exposure a measure of reporting practice as much as of tumour biology
The cystic-calcified cell that anchors the four-way survival comparison contains 16 patients, and that comparison carries p = 0.043 with no correction for the multiple pairwise contrasts implied

Median follow-up is 35 months in a disease whose recurrences arrive at a median of 4-7 years, so every 5-year recurrence-free survival figure is extrapolated from a thin risk set, and the stated last follow-up date of March 2017 is the same year the accrual window closes

The conclusion that these features could inform the decision to observe or resect a small asymptomatic PNET is drawn from a cohort in which no patient was observed - the authors acknowledge they cannot identify the non-operated patients and then make the recommendation anyway
Cystic morphology, one of the paper's two headline features, was not independently prognostic (p = 0.69), yet the abstract and conclusion present both features as usable for stratification
36434481.n: 981 patients resected for well-differentiated PNET; cystic morphology data missing in 279 (28%) and calcification data missing in 284 (29%)
36434481.bottom_line: Across 981 resected well-differentiated pancreatic NET, radiographic calcification marked adverse pathology and shorter recurrence-free survival while a predominantly cystic appearance marked the opposite, but calcification's independent hazard ratio of 11.5 spans 1.1 to 125.0, cystic morphology was not independent at all, nearly 30% of the exposure data are missing, and nobody in the cohort was observed.

limitations: The preamble states that the standard is not an inflexible rule or requirement of practice, is not intended to establish a legal standard of care, and the societies caution against its use in litigation
Adherence to the standard will not ensure an accurate diagnosis or a successful outcome; all that should be expected is a reasonable course of action based on current knowledge

SUV measurements may not be reproducible across scanners and institutions without standardisation of imaging protocols, scanner qualification and cross-calibration, and SUV is affected by lesion size and uptake time
It is unclear how SSTR PET should be used for selecting patients for PRRT because NETTER-1 enrolled patients on the basis of 111In-pentetreotide rather than PET
It is currently unclear whether delayed imaging with 64Cu-DOTATATE offers benefit over standard times

It is difficult to generalise how much of 68Ga's greater positron range will affect quantification in small lesions because of the complex interplay of detector resolution, system diameter, reconstruction algorithm and spatial filtering
critique: The document asserts that the three tracers can be considered equivalent for detecting SSTR-positive disease while in the same text quantifying a 10-20% SUV underestimation for 68Ga in 10-15 mm lesions and a five-fold count deficit for 64Cu; claims of equivalence and of measurable difference sit side by side with no head-to-head outcome data resolving them, which matters most for exactly the sub-centimetre pancreatic lesion a pathway is deciding about

There is no systematic review, no evidence grading and no strength-of-recommendation scheme, so a prospective trial, an expert opinion and an FDA package insert carry identical typographic authority, and the package inserts are cited repeatedly as primary sources for dosing and uptake timing

The instruction to discontinue long-acting somatostatin analogues 3-4 weeks before imaging is carried over from the EANM guideline while the adjacent text cites prospective evidence that this is unnecessary for lanreotide - leaving the reader with two contradictory instructions and no recommendation

Several authors hold intellectual property or consultancy relationships with the manufacturers of the tracers being standardised - one is named in a later ENETS document as inventor/IPR holder on 64Cu-DOTATATE - and the text of this version carries no individual disclosure statement, only a blanket line that no potential conflict was reported

Physiological uptake in the pancreatic head and uncinate process is the single largest source of false positives for any pancreatic pathway, and the standard acknowledges that its SUVs overlap with tumour but offers no decision rule beyond correlating with MRI or multiphase CT and following up

The standard is silent on whether SSTR PET should be performed at all for a sub-2 cm incidental pancreatic lesion under surveillance, and silent on whether serial SSTR PET has any role in surveillance - while simultaneously warning that change in uptake must not be read as response or progression, which removes the obvious use
The appropriate use criteria that define the indications are cited rather than reproduced, so the document that governs when to order the test does not itself contain the indications
Dosimetry is tabulated from four separate historical publications of varying vintage and method and presented as a single comparative table
36725249.bottom_line: The authoritative technical standard for acquiring, interpreting and reporting somatostatin receptor PET, including tracer dosimetry, the modified Krenning score and the pancreatic head uptake trap - but it is consensus without evidence grading, it calls three physically unequal tracers equivalent, and it gives no guidance on whether or how to use SSTR PET in a small pancreatic lesion under surveillance.

limitations: The authors state only that their many years of experience in the field are still being verified in the light of results from new clinical studies, which set new ways of proceeding
Treatment of NF-Pan-NEN still requires the decision of a multidisciplinary team of neuroendocrine neoplasm specialists, and ENETS Centres of Excellence should be strongly considered
Further studies are needed to fulfil unmet needs, focusing on prognostic molecular markers, the selection of a therapeutic approach and the sequence of treatments
Data sharing is not applicable as no new data were created or analysed

Specific uncertainties acknowledged in the text: no validated consensus on the definition of resectability; no preoperative examination accurately predicts nodal involvement; robust data on radiofrequency ablation and on minimally invasive pancreaticoduodenectomy are lacking; no evidence supports somatostatin analogues for controlling progression of small NF-Pan-NET under surveillance; the role of chemotherapy as adjuvant therapy is unknown; limited data exist on PRRT for G3
critique: The two recommendations that most change practice - surveillance for lesions of 1 cm or less and surgery for everything above 2 cm - both carry level 3 evidence and grade B, yet the second is written in the imperative ('strongly recommended'), and the 1-2 cm band into which most incidental lesions fall is handed back to the clinician with no decision rule at all

The follow-up schedule and the recommendation to surveil for at least 20 years and possibly lifelong rest on level 5 evidence - expert opinion without explicit critical appraisal, by the paper's own table - while being assigned grade B, an inversion the GRADE framework the paper claims to follow would not permit

PANDORA and the ASPEN interim analysis are cited as the prospective basis for surveillance at median follow-ups of 17 and 25 months, without the document noting that both are far shorter than the 7-year median time to pancreatic recurrence and the 12-18% recurrence rate it reports elsewhere in the same text

The ASPEN principal investigator and the author of the ENETS surgical guideline being operationalised are among the authors, so the guidance grades evidence its own authors generated, and ASPEN was itself funded by ENETS

CLARINET's hazard ratio in the pancreatic subgroup crosses unity (0.58, 95% CI 0.32-1.04) and is cited in support of a grade A recommendation for upfront somatostatin analogues - a confidence interval that does not exclude no effect supporting the strongest grade available

Belzutifan's 90.9% response figure is imported from a single-arm 22-patient secondary endpoint in VHL disease and placed in a nonfunctioning sporadic pancreatic NET guideline, with the caveat about metastatic disease but not about the design

The E2211 chemotherapy recommendation is built on a PFS advantage with non-significant response and overall survival, in a trial limited to Ki-67 up to 20%, and is then extended to G3 disease on the strength of one retrospective series (evidence 3b, grade B)
There is no systematic search, no evidence table and no description of how the literature informing each question was selected, so the level-of-evidence labels cannot be audited

Eleven of the thirteen authors declare consultancy, speaker or advisory relationships with the manufacturers of the recommended agents - Ipsen, Novartis, AAA, Pfizer, MSD among them - and one holds intellectual property on 64Cu-DOTATATE, the tracer whose superior lesion detection the imaging section endorses
37877341.bottom_line: The current ENETS position on nonfunctioning pancreatic NET: observe lesions of 1 cm or less, individualise 1-2 cm, operate above 2 cm or with duct dilation, stage with SSTR-PET/CT and surveil for twenty years or more - sensible, practical and widely followed, but the pivotal surgical thresholds carry level 3 evidence, the follow-up schedule carries level 5, and the prospective studies invoked have two years of follow-up.

limitations: The recommendations are limited by the varying methodological quality of available data, derived primarily from retrospective series and insufficient to provide high or moderate certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach
Only 37 of 3048 publications (1.2%) met the inclusion criteria for the systematic reviews

Confounding could have arisen in the surgery versus surveillance comparison because surgery for tumours of 2 cm or less was indicated by growth on serial imaging, so the effects of surgery may have been underestimated; given that the implications of surveillance for morbidity, metastasis and mortality are important and irreversible, a more cautious approach might be prudent
Further studies are required to validate and optimise the proposed screening protocols and to develop shared decision-making tools
A similar evidence-based and consensus-based approach is still required for adrenal tumours, which are frequently found as incidentalomas on surveillance MRI

Biomarkers are lacking for accurate risk stratification of neuroendocrine tumours, for predicting aggressive pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, for personalised risk-based management and for early detection of thymic neuroendocrine tumours

Better variant-of-uncertain-significance prediction tools and high-throughput functional assays are needed for genetic testing; prospective, well-annotated cohorts with clinical biobanks and global collaboration are needed to enable the research
critique: The systematic review found no difference between surgery and surveillance for lesions of 2 cm or less, and the panel then declines to follow its own finding, writing that 'a more cautious approach might be prudent' - a defensible clinical judgement, but it means the resulting operative posture is expert preference overriding the evidence the exercise was convened to produce, and should not be cited as evidence-based

1814 patients across 37 mostly retrospective studies for an entire multi-organ syndrome means every pancreatic statement rests on very few events; the panel's own GRADE rating is low or very low throughout while the statements are worded as recommendations carrying 92-100% agreement

A Delphi percentage measures how many experts agree, not how likely they are to be right; the paper's own scale calls 51% agreement a 'consider', so the apparatus systematically converts low-certainty evidence into high-confidence prose, and the agreement figure is the only number most readers will carry away

The 1 mm per year growth criterion in statements 28 and 39 has no cited derivation and lies below the measurement reproducibility of serial MRI of a multifocal pancreas across different scanners and readers, so it will generate both false stability and false progression

Panel selection was by recognised standing within the same societies that issued the 2001 and 2012 guidelines, and several authors wrote those, so the 'new or now explicit' labels partly re-endorse the panel's own prior positions

Recommending pancreatic MRI from age 10-15 commits asymptomatic children to lifelong imaging on the strength of penetrance data alone, with no outcome evidence that earlier detection reduces mortality and no analysis of the harms - incidental adrenal findings, which the paper separately flags as a growing problem, or the psychological burden of surveillance from childhood

The screening recommendations deliberately aim to detect 'clinically relevant disease, and not necessarily the earliest onset of disease', yet the interval recommendations are set by expert vote with no modelling of what interval achieves that distinction

Nothing in this document transfers to sporadic nonfunctioning pancreatic NET: in MEN1 the gland carries a field defect, lesions are multiple, patients are decades younger, and competing parathyroid, pituitary and thymic disease dominates the risk calculus - so the MEN1 2 cm threshold and the sporadic 2 cm threshold happen to share a number but not an evidence base
40523372.n: 55 recommendations, comprising 52 Delphi consensus statements plus 3 from systematic reviews of 37 of 3048 publications covering 1814 patients
40523372.bottom_line: The most rigorous MEN1 guidance yet assembled, and its most important finding for a pancreatic pathway is negative: across 37 usable studies, surgery and active surveillance for nonfunctioning pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours of 2 cm or less produced no difference in metastasis or mortality at low or very low GRADE certainty - after which the panel recommends caution anyway, on expert judgement rather than data.
